doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Abart's trio with Louis Powers and Harold Minor
summary: She took a trio to Abart's on 9th Street for about a year, and fumbles the dates.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: So did this gig eventually lead to that gig, and were there gigs in between?

Well, no, that was the beginning, and then there‘s a place called . . . on 9th Street . . . Abart‘s [phonetic]. We had done 7-T, so let me go in and check that. I just went there and same thing, and the mom and dad liked me, and they were building this place. And I said, ―I‘d like to have the job.‖ So then there was a trio, right.
That you brought to that?
Yeah. I took a trio in there.
The same group of musicians, some of the same musicians?
No, no, no. It was Harold Minor and Louis Powers.
Was this the beginning of your . . . this was your first trio, the first serious trio?
I think so, yeah, yeah. So then we did that, and I think stayed about a year.
What age were you then?
I don‘t remember.
Or what year? If you remember the year . . .
Don‘t start that. [laughs]
I know. But just [unclear].
I‘m trying to think now, what year. I tell you what. I‘ll get it together. Okay.
Just so you know, and it‘s not necessarily correct, but I have here that . . . I had a year here.
Oh, just leave them alone.
1954, roughly, for the year of your first group.
No, indeed.
Okay, so then that‘s wrong.
No, that‘s wrong, child. Fifty-four? [makes razzing sound.]
Is that too late? That‘s what we need to know . . .
No, that‘s too early. No, that‘s too . . . no, that‘s ‘54? Good lord, I was . . . I‘m going to tell my mother.
Well, you‘re twenty.
We‘ll talk about that later.
Okay.
Okay, go on, go on now.
You were telling me about this Abart‘s.
Yes, Abart‘s. Anyway, that was Louis Powers and Harold Minor.
Harold Minor on base, and Louis Powers on . . .
Louis Powers on bass, and Harold on drums. Now, I‘m going to tell you when that was. That was . . . good lord. Remember the Three Sounds?
Yes, I do remember.
Okay. They were next door at the Hollywood, upstairs. In fact, we were just talking about that the other day. Oh, man.
Do you remember where you met Louis and . . .

Harold. I don‘t remember. Let‘s see, Louis was working with the State Department. Harold was working in the government. I don‘t remember. I can‘t tell you. But this is a long . . . do we have to go that far? Let‘s go on to something else, okay, because I can‘t . . .
